response.title: which 3d scanner is the fastest for scanning a big car part
response.answer:
For scanning a large automotive part as quickly as possible, I'd focus on industrial handheld 3D laser scanners rather than consumer scanners.

The fastest scanner on paper isn't necessarily the fastest in practice. For large car parts—such as bumpers, doors, hoods, chassis components, or entire body panels—the important factors are:

Scanning speed: How many 3D measurements the scanner captures per second.

Field of view: How much surface it captures in one pass.

Tracking: Whether you need to place reference markers on the part.

Accuracy: Whether you need reverse-engineering accuracy or just a usable 3D model.

My top 3 recommendations
Shop

1. SCANOLOGY TrackScan Sharp-Z

Highest published measurement rate here

10 million measurements/sec

Up to 800 × 700 mm scanning area, marker-free optical tracking, and 12 m tracking distance. Excellent for large automotive assemblies. 
Rapid Scan 3D

Shop

2. SCANOLOGY KSCAN-E

8.29 million measurements/sec

Up to 1,440 × 1,000 mm scanning area. Particularly attractive for large hoods, bumpers, and body panels. 
SCANOLOGY
+1

Shop

3. Creaform HandySCAN MAX Elite

2.25 million measurements/sec

Up to approximately 2 × 2.4 m scanning area. Designed for very large parts, with a wide capture area that can reduce the number of passes. 
Creaform 3D

These are manufacturer-published specifications, not independently measured end-to-end scan times. The Sharp-Z has the highest stated point rate among these three, but the KSCAN-E or HandySCAN MAX could finish a particular part sooner because of their larger scanning areas.
